free_tier.stated: Test projects grant a computing-time budget on JURECA, the JUWELS cluster or the JUPITER Booster for up to four months, optionally with about two person-weeks of expert support from a JSC Simulation and Data Lab, with applications accepted throughout the year.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: The two person-weeks of SDL porting support is worth more than the node hours for a solo applicant, and it is the one JSC tier that would help a code become competitive, but it is behind German employment.

limits.value: Applications may be filed only by applicants employed at a university or research facility in Germany, so the nationality bar is zero and the German employment bar is absolute.

evidence.proved: 'applications for test projects with or without extended support may be filed by applicants who are employed at a university or research facility in Germany (irrespective of the applicant's nationality)', quoted
'a period of up to four months'; 'Applications for test projects on JSC resources may be submitted throughout the year'; SDL support 'around 2 person-weeks per project', quoted

'Eligible are scientists with affiliations of German universities or research facilities. Here, the nationality of the applicant is irrelevant'; 'Test access to JUWELS for the preparation of Regular Project applications is available', quoted

record.notes: JSC publishes no core-hour figure for test projects: the page says 'a certain number of core-hours' and never quantifies it, so the field is null rather than guessed. The extended-support variant is the unusual offer, because a Simulation and Data Lab contributes staff time, which is the scarce input for a solo researcher. The explicit sentence that nationality is irrelevant while German employment is required is the cleanest statement of the binding constraint found in the German stack.
